stories.headline: Spain's 'No to War' stance on Iran conflict creates tensions with US and Trump
stories.summary: Pedro Sánchez maintains Spain's 'No a la guerra' position regarding the Iran conflict, prohibiting US use of Spanish military bases for strikes on Iran and drawing criticism from Trump while gaining international support. Sánchez scheduled to appear in Congress on March 25 to explain Spain's position.

stories.headline: PP wins Castilla y León elections, still needs Vox support while PSOE gains seats
stories.summary: Alfonso Fernández Mañueco (PP) wins the March 15 Castilla y León regional elections but remains dependent on Vox for governance. PSOE candidate Carlos Martínez gains two seats despite predictions of losses, while Vox falls short of expectations at under 20% of vote.

stories.headline: King Felipe VI conducts diplomatic tour of Portugal, Chile and Bolivia as government ministers skip events
stories.summary: King Felipe VI attends presidential inaugurations in Portugal (António José Seguro) and Chile (José Antonio Kast) as part of a multi-country diplomatic tour. Foreign Minister Albares cancels his participation in Chile trip, leaving the King to represent Spain alone at key events.

stories.headline: ERC blocks Catalan budget approval demanding IRPF tax collection transfer from Madrid
stories.summary: Esquerra Republicana refuses to support Salvador Illa's Catalan budget unless the central government transfers collection of personal income tax (IRPF) to Catalonia. Negotiations remain deadlocked with budget vote scheduled for March 20.

stories.headline: Vox faces internal crisis as Ortega Smith expelled and Abascal consolidates control
stories.summary: Vox experiences internal upheaval with party co-founder Javier Ortega Smith expelled from leadership roles after challenging Santiago Abascal. Other regional leaders like José Ángel Antelo in Murcia also face disciplinary action as Abascal centralizes party control.

stories.headline: Government creates HODIO tool to measure hate and polarization online
stories.summary: Pedro Sánchez announces creation of HODIO (Huella del Odio y la Polarización), a new government tool designed to measure and combat hate speech and polarization on social media platforms. Critics question its implications for free speech.

stories.headline: Yolanda Díaz travels to Oscars amid government crisis negotiations
stories.summary: Deputy PM Yolanda Díaz travels to Los Angeles to attend the Academy Awards ceremony representing the Spanish government, drawing criticism for the timing amid Iran war crisis and internal government tensions over economic measures.

stories.headline: Minor parties seek to reform Congress rules to guarantee parliamentary groups
stories.summary: ERC, Junts, Podemos, Compromís and BNG register a proposal to reform Congress regulations, lowering the thresholds required to form parliamentary groups from 5% to 3% nationally and from 15% to 10% regionally to avoid relegation to Mixed Group.

stories.headline: Hamas praises Spanish government for downgrading ambassador to Israel
stories.summary: Hamas and Houthi rebels issue statements praising Pedro Sánchez's government for reducing diplomatic representation in Israel by ceasing ambassador Ana María Sálomon. Critics point to Spain's growing isolation from NATO allies.
